title: Tech Stocks Fall as Investors Want Proof on AI Spending
summary: Friday, October 30, 2026, was a rough day for many technology stocks. Investors worried that excitement about artificial intelligence, or AI, had pushed some prices too high. A stock is a small piece of a company. The S&P 500 fell about 1.8 percent, its worst single day since June. The Nasdaq dropped 2.9 percent. Chipmaker Intel fell 28.6 percent, its worst drop since 1974. Intel reported stronger profit than experts expected, but its forecast for the final three months of the year was lower than experts expected. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said the personal-computer industry continues to feel pressure. Amazon fell 1.4 percent after weaker summer profit and heavy AI spending. The day before, Alphabet, the company behind Google and YouTube, had dropped more than 12 percent after spending more cash in the summer than in the spring, also largely on AI. Portfolio manager Joe Tigay said investors now want clearer proof that the spending will pay off. Not every stock fell: ExxonMobil rose 2.2 percent and Chevron added 1.8 percent after stronger summer profit than experts expected.
why_it_matters: It matters because the companies behind the computers, phones, and videos you use can lose value when grown-ups decide whether new technology is worth what it costs.

background_read: A stock is a small piece of a company, and people buy stocks hoping the company will do well and the piece will become worth more.
Artificial intelligence is a kind of computer technology that can learn and do tasks, and many big technology companies are spending a lot of money to build it.
When investors worry that prices have risen too high or that the spending may not pay off soon, they may sell stocks, and that selling can make prices fall.
